title: Stage 1 listening stories
intro: Short listening stories built from Stage 1 of the versatility list. Stories 1–9 go from easiest to hardest; stories 10–13 are practice stories built around the Stage 1 words the first nine use least (greetings, degree words, polite past forms, sequencing). For each one: listen without looking at any text, answer the five questions, then open Answers and transcript to check. Each line gives the Japanese for your voice tool, with the speaker and a voice hint; if the voice misreads a kanji, use the kana version of that line instead. Words outside Stage 1 are listed under New words.

stories.title: Bumping into a friend
stories.setting: Old friends Yuki and Kenta run into each other on a Tokyo street: he is on his way to work, and she is on her way to a shop.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: yuki! hisashiburi!
lines.ja: ユキ！久しぶり！
lines.kana: ゆき！ひさしぶり！

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenta! hisashiburi da ne! ima kara doko iku no?
lines.ja: ケンタ！久しぶりだね！今からどこ行くの？
lines.kana: けんた！ひさしぶりだね！いまからどこいくの？
lines.english: Kenta! It's been ages! Where are you off to now?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: kaisha. yuki wa? uchi ni kaeru no?
lines.ja: 会社。ユキは？うちに帰るの？
lines.kana: かいしゃ。ゆきは？うちにかえるの？

lines.kana: ほんとに？じゃあ、きょうはうちにかえる。

lines.kana: うん。あしたはやってるよ。

lines.ja: 明日行くね。ありがとう、じゃあね！
lines.kana: あしたいくね。ありがとう、じゃあね！
lines.english: I'll go tomorrow, then. Thanks, see you!

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: jaa ne!
lines.ja: じゃあね！
lines.kana: じゃあね！
lines.english: See you!

newWords.english: (of a shop) is open, doing business; from yaru

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Yuki and Kenta go to the shop together today.
The shop is closed today, so Yuki will go tomorrow.
Kenta's office is closed today, so he goes home.

questions.explanation: Line 4: Yuki is heading to the shop over there. Line 7: Kenta tells her it's closed today (kyou wa yasumi). Line 8: she decides to go home today (kyou wa uchi ni kaeru). Line 10: she'll go tomorrow (ashita iku ne). A is wrong because Kenta is going to work (line 3) and they say goodbye (lines 10-11). C is wrong because the shop is the thing that's closed (yasumi, line 7), and Kenta is on his way to his company (line 3).

questions.english: Where is Kenta going?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは、どこに行きますか？
questions.kana: けんたさんは、どこにいきますか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, doko ni ikimasu ka?

choices.english: To his office
Home
To the shop

questions.explanation: Line 3: Kenta answers 'kaisha', his company, so he's going to work. 'uchi ni kaeru no?' in the same line is his guess about Yuki, not his own plan. The shop is where Yuki was going (line 4). Kenta has just come from there (line 7: ima asoko kara kita n da), and he isn't going back.

questions.english: Why was Yuki going to the shop?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、なんでその店に行くんですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、なんでそのみせにいくんですか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, nande sono mise ni iku n desu ka?

choices.english: The shop is only open today.
She has the day off today.
She's out of tea at home.

questions.explanation: Line 5: Kenta asks 'nande?'. Line 6: Yuki answers 'uchi ni ocha ga mou nai n da': there's no tea left at home, and n da gives it as her reason. A is the opposite of what happens: the shop is closed today and open tomorrow (lines 7 and 9). B misplaces yasumi: in line 7 the shop is the thing that's closed (yasumi), and no one says Yuki has a day off.

questions.english: Kenta says, "demo, ano mise, kyou wa yasumi da yo." What does he mean by ending with "yo"?
questions.ja: 「今日は休みだよ。」ここの「よ」は、何ですか？
questions.kana: 「きょうはやすみだよ。」ここの「よ」は、なんですか？
questions.romaji: "kyou wa yasumi da yo." koko no "yo" wa, nan desu ka?

choices.english: He's checking something they both already know.
He's telling Yuki something she doesn't know yet.
He's wondering out loud whether the shop is open.

questions.explanation: Line 7: yo marks news for the listener. Yuki didn't know: she was on her way there (lines 4-6) and reacts with 'honto ni?' (line 8). Kenta is sure because he just came from there (ima asoko kara kita n da). To check something they both know, he would say 'yo ne' (A). To wonder out loud, he would say 'kana' (C).

questions.english: Yuki asks Kenta, "ima kara doko iku no?" Imagine she asks you. What could you say back?
questions.ja: 今からどこ行くの？
questions.kana: いまからどこいくの？
questions.romaji: ima kara doko iku no?
questions.answer: Say where you're going now (home, over there). Maybe give a reason with n da, or ask her back with '... wa?'

modelAnswers.romaji: uchi ni kaeru yo. yuki wa?
modelAnswers.ja: うちに帰るよ。ユキは？
modelAnswers.english: I'm going home. How about you, Yuki?

modelAnswers.romaji: asoko ni iku n da. yuki mo kuru?
modelAnswers.ja: あそこに行くんだ。ユキも来る？
modelAnswers.english: I'm heading over there. Want to come too, Yuki?

questions.explanation: Yuki asks Kenta this in line 2. His answer in line 3 ('kaisha. yuki wa?') shows the pattern: name the place, then ask back with '... wa?'. The Japanese prompt is Yuki's casual line itself, not a polite question, because you are answering her as a friend.

stories.title: Sorry I'm late
stories.setting: Mai rushes up late to meet her friend Sora in town, apologises, and hands him a coffee she brought.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, 20s, bright, a little out of breath

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora! mada ita! gomen, chotto osoku natchatta!
lines.ja: ソラ！まだいた！ごめん、ちょっと遅くなっちゃった！
lines.kana: そら！まだいた！ごめん、ちょっとおそくなっちゃった！
lines.english: Sora! You're still here! Sorry, I'm a bit late!

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii yo, ii yo. daijoubu.
lines.ja: いいよ、いいよ。大丈夫。
lines.kana: いいよ、いいよ。だいじょうぶ。
lines.english: It's fine, it's fine. No problem.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: datte, densha ga zutto konakatta kara.
lines.ja: だって、電車がずっと来なかったから。
lines.kana: だって、でんしゃがずっとこなかったから。
lines.english: It's just, the train wouldn't come.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: densha ka. dakara osoku natta n da. jaa, mai wa warukunai yo.
lines.ja: 電車か。だから遅くなったんだ。じゃあ、マイは悪くないよ。
lines.kana: でんしゃか。だからおそくなったんだ。じゃあ、まいはわるくないよ。
lines.english: The train, huh. So that's why you were late. Then it's not your fault.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sora wa, itsu kita no?
lines.ja: ソラは、いつ来たの？
lines.kana: そらは、いつきたの？
lines.english: And when did you get here, Sora?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: mou zutto matteta yo. chotto ja nai yo ne.
lines.ja: もうずっと待ってたよ。ちょっとじゃないよね。
lines.kana: もうずっとまってたよ。ちょっとじゃないよね。
lines.english: I've been waiting the whole time. That's not "a bit," is it?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: honto ni gomen ne. kore, douzo.
lines.ja: ほんとにごめんね。これ、どうぞ。
lines.kana: ほんとにごめんね。これ、どうぞ。
lines.english: I'm really sorry. Here, this is for you.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, sore nani?
lines.ja: え、それ何？
lines.kana: え、それなに？
lines.english: Huh? What's that?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: koohii. sora ni motte kita n da.
lines.ja: コーヒー。ソラに持ってきたんだ。
lines.kana: コーヒー。そらにもってきたんだ。
lines.english: Coffee. I brought it for you.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii no? arigatou! jaa, iku?
lines.ja: いいの？ありがとう！じゃあ、行く？
lines.kana: いいの？ありがとう！じゃあ、いく？
lines.english: For me? Thanks! Okay, shall we go?

newWords.english: late, slow (osoku natchatta = I ended up late; osoku natta = got late)
huh? (surprise, rising tone; not the particle e)

questions.english: What happens in this story?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Sora is late, and Mai is annoyed that she had to wait.
Mai is late, says sorry, and gives Sora something she brought.
Mai and Sora wait together for a train that never comes.

questions.explanation: Line 1: Mai says gomen, chotto osoku natchatta (sorry, I'm a bit late). Lines 7-9: she hands Sora something (kore, douzo), and it turns out to be a coffee. A swaps the two people: Sora is the one who waited (line 6). C mixes up the train: only Mai's train wouldn't come (line 3), and they never wait for one together.

questions.english: What did Mai bring for Sora?
questions.ja: マイさんは、ソラさんに何を持ってきましたか？
questions.kana: まいさんは、そらさんになにをもってきましたか？
questions.romaji: mai-san wa, sora-san ni nani o motte kimashita ka?

choices.english: A train ticket she didn't use.
A coffee she bought for herself.
A coffee that she brought for him.

questions.explanation: Line 9: koohii. sora ni motte kita n da (Coffee. I brought it for you). Sora ni means it's for him, and in line 10 he asks ii no? (For me?) and thanks her. B is wrong because the coffee is for Sora, not for her. A is wrong because the train only comes up as her excuse (line 3), and she never gives him a ticket.

questions.english: When did Sora get there?
questions.ja: ソラさんは、いつ来ましたか？
questions.kana: そらさんは、いつきましたか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa, itsu kimashita ka?

choices.english: Long before Mai. He'd been waiting the whole time.
Only a little before Mai, so he didn't wait long.
He was late too, because his train didn't come.

questions.explanation: Line 5: Mai asks sora wa, itsu kita no? (when did you get here?). Line 6: Sora doesn't give a time. He says mou zutto matteta yo (I've been waiting the whole time), then chotto ja nai yo ne (that's not 'a bit', is it?), turning Mai's own chotto from line 1 back on her. Line 1 (mada ita! = you're still here!) also shows he was there first. B repeats that chotto, which Sora says isn't true. C mixes up the train: only Mai's train wouldn't come (line 3).

questions.english: Mai says "datte, densha ga zutto konakatta kara." What is she doing with "datte"?
questions.ja: マイさんの「だって、電車がずっと来なかったから」。この「だって」で、マイさんは何をしてますか？
questions.kana: まいさんの「だって、でんしゃがずっとこなかったから」。この「だって」で、まいさんはなにをしてますか？
questions.romaji: mai-san no 'datte, densha ga zutto konakatta kara'. kono 'datte' de, mai-san wa nani o shitemasu ka?

choices.english: Drawing a conclusion: the train didn't come, so let's go now.
Making an excuse: it's not her fault, the train didn't come.
Asking a question: did Sora's train not come either?

questions.explanation: Line 3: datte opens an excuse ('it's just that...'), and kara at the end gives the reason: the train wouldn't come. Sora accepts it in line 4: jaa, mai wa warukunai yo (then it's not your fault). A describes dakara ('so'), which draws a conclusion. Sora uses it that way in line 4 (dakara osoku natta n da = so that's why you were late), and it's Sora, not Mai, who suggests going (line 10). C is wrong because the line ends in kara without a rising question tone, and nobody mentions Sora's train.

questions.english: Sora teases Mai: "mou zutto matteta yo. chotto ja nai yo ne." If you were Mai, what could you say back?
questions.ja: 「もうずっと待ってたよ。ちょっとじゃないよね」って、ソラさんが。マイさんは？
questions.kana: 「もうずっとまってたよ。ちょっとじゃないよね」って、そらさんが。まいさんは？
questions.romaji: 'mou zutto matteta yo. chotto ja nai yo ne' tte, sora-san ga. mai-san wa?
questions.answer: Apologise again, warmly, e.g. 'honto ni gomen ne.' or 'gomen. watashi ga warukatta.'

modelAnswers.romaji: honto ni gomen ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ほんとにごめんね。
modelAnswers.english: I'm really sorry.

modelAnswers.romaji: gomen. watashi ga warukatta.
modelAnswers.ja: ごめん。私が悪かった。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry. That was my fault.

questions.explanation: Line 6 is a friendly tease, not real anger: he already said ii yo, daijoubu in line 2 and mai wa warukunai yo in line 4. The natural comeback is another apology, the way Mai does in line 7 (honto ni gomen ne). warukatta is the past of warui: 'I was the one at fault.'

stories.title: Whose is this?
stories.setting: At home, Kenta finds an umbrella, a key and a bag lying around and asks his flatmate Sora whose they are.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: sora, kono kasa, dare no?
lines.ja: ソラ、この傘、誰の？
lines.kana: そら、このかさ、だれの？
lines.english: Sora, whose umbrella is this?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: sore, watashi no! doko ni atta no?
lines.ja: それ、私の！どこにあったの？
lines.kana: それ、わたしの！どこにあったの？
lines.english: That's mine! Where was it?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: asoko ni atta yo. jaa, kono kagi wa? kore mo sora no?
lines.ja: あそこにあったよ。じゃあ、この鍵は？これもソラの？
lines.kana: あそこにあったよ。じゃあ、このかぎは？これもそらの？
lines.english: It was over there. Okay, what about this key? Is this yours too?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: uun, watashi no ja nai yo. jibun no kagi, motteru shi.
lines.ja: ううん、私のじゃないよ。自分の鍵、持ってるし。
lines.kana: ううん、わたしのじゃないよ。じぶんのかぎ、もってるし。
lines.english: No, it's not mine. I've got my own key, anyway.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: boku no mo koko ni aru shi. dare no kana.
lines.ja: 僕のもここにあるし。誰のかな。
lines.kana: ぼくのもここにあるし。だれのかな。
lines.english: And mine's right here, so it's not mine either. I wonder whose it is.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: sono kagi, mai no da yo. kinou, mai-tachi, uchi ni kita yo ne.
lines.ja: その鍵、マイのだよ。昨日、マイたち、うちに来たよね。
lines.kana: そのかぎ、まいのだよ。きのう、まいたち、うちにきたよね。
lines.english: That key's Mai's. Mai and the others came over yesterday, right?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un, kita ne. ato, are wa? ano kaban.
lines.ja: うん、来たね。あと、あれは？あのかばん。
lines.kana: うん、きたね。あと、あれは？あのかばん。
lines.english: Yeah, they did. Oh, and what about that? That bag over there.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: dore? asoko no? are wa watashi no ja nai yo. kenta no?
lines.ja: どれ？あそこの？あれは私のじゃないよ。ケンタの？
lines.kana: どれ？あそこの？あれはわたしのじゃないよ。けんたの？
lines.english: Which one? The one over there? That's not mine. Is it yours?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: uun, boku no ja nai. mai-san-tachi, ano kaban motteta kke?
lines.ja: ううん、僕のじゃない。マイさんたち、あのかばん持ってたっけ？
lines.kana: ううん、ぼくのじゃない。まいさんたち、あのかばんもってたっけ？
lines.english: No, not mine. Did Mai and the others have that bag with them? I can't quite remember.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: iya, mottenakatta naa. demo, ashita minna ni kiitoku ne.
lines.ja: いや、持ってなかったなあ。でも、明日みんなに聞いとくね。
lines.kana: いや、もってなかったなあ。でも、あしたみんなにきいとくね。
lines.english: Nah, I don't think they had it. But I'll ask everyone tomorrow.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un, onegai. kono kagi wa boku ga mottoku yo.
lines.ja: うん、お願い。この鍵は僕が持っとくよ。
lines.kana: うん、おねがい。このかぎはぼくがもっとくよ。
lines.english: Yeah, please. I'll hang on to this key for now.

questions.english: What are Kenta and Sora doing in this conversation?
questions.ja: ケンタさんとソラさんは、何をしてますか？
questions.kana: けんたさんとそらさんは、なにをしてますか？
questions.romaji: kenta-san to sora-san wa, nani o shitemasu ka?

choices.english: Sora has lost her key and asks Kenta to help find it.
Kenta and Sora are planning to have Mai and her friends over tomorrow.
Kenta finds things at home, and they try to work out whose they are.

questions.explanation: Kenta keeps asking whose things are: the umbrella (line 1), the key (line 3) and the bag (line 7). The umbrella is Sora's (line 2), the key is Mai's (line 6), and nobody knows about the bag (lines 8-10). A is wrong because Sora says she has her own key (line 4). B is wrong because Mai's group came yesterday (line 6). Tomorrow is only when Sora will ask everyone about the bag (line 10).

questions.english: Whose is the key Kenta found?
questions.ja: うちにあった鍵は、誰のですか？
questions.kana: うちにあったかぎは、だれのですか？
questions.romaji: uchi ni atta kagi wa, dare no desu ka?

choices.english: Mai's
Sora's
Kenta's

questions.explanation: In line 4 Sora says it isn't hers because she has her own key ('jibun no kagi, motteru shi'). In line 5 Kenta says his own key is right here, so it isn't his either. In line 6 Sora says 'sono kagi, mai no da yo' (that key is Mai's).

questions.english: What will Sora do tomorrow?
questions.ja: ソラさんは、明日何をしますか？
questions.kana: そらさんは、あしたなにをしますか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa, ashita nani o shimasu ka?

choices.english: Keep the key for Mai
Have Mai and the others over again
Ask everyone about the bag

questions.explanation: In line 10 Sora says 'demo, ashita minna ni kiitoku ne' (but I'll ask everyone tomorrow). She means the bag that nobody can place (lines 8-9). Keeping the key is what Kenta says he'll do (line 11). Mai's group already came over yesterday (line 6), and nobody plans another visit.

questions.english: Near the end, Kenta asks 'mai-san-tachi, ano kaban motteta kke?' What does the 'kke' at the end show?
questions.ja: 持ってたっけって、何ですか？
questions.kana: もってたっけって、なんですか？
questions.romaji: motteta kke tte, nan desu ka?

choices.english: He is sure they had the bag and is telling Sora.
He is trying to remember, and wants Sora to help him recall.
He thinks they had the bag and wants Sora to agree.

questions.explanation: 'kke' marks something you are trying to remember ('did they ... again?'). In line 9 Kenta can't recall whether Mai's group had that bag, so he checks with Sora. In line 10 she says 'iya, mottenakatta naa' (nah, I don't think they had it). He isn't telling her (that would be 'motteta yo'). He also doesn't believe they had it and want her to agree (that would be 'motteta yo ne?').

questions.english: Imagine Kenta holds up the umbrella and asks you 'kono kasa, dare no?', but it isn't yours. What could you say back?
questions.ja: この傘、誰の？
questions.kana: このかさ、だれの？
questions.romaji: kono kasa, dare no?
questions.answer: Say it isn't yours (watashi no / boku no ja nai) and wonder whose it is (dare no kana) or guess someone else's (sora no ja nai no?).

modelAnswers.romaji: uun, watashi no ja nai yo. dare no kana.
modelAnswers.ja: ううん、私のじゃないよ。誰のかな。
modelAnswers.english: No, it's not mine. I wonder whose it is.

modelAnswers.romaji: boku no ja nai yo. sora no ja nai no?
modelAnswers.ja: 僕のじゃないよ。ソラのじゃないの？
modelAnswers.english: It's not mine. Isn't it Sora's?

questions.explanation: The story uses this pattern several times. Line 4 has 'watashi no ja nai yo', line 8 'are wa watashi no ja nai yo', line 9 'boku no ja nai', and line 5 'dare no kana'. Put them together to say it isn't yours and wonder or guess whose it is.

stories.title: A voicemail
stories.setting: On a rainy evening, Kenta leaves a phone message for his friend Yuki to change their plan for tomorrow.

speakers.name: Kenta
speakers.voice: male, late 20s, warm and friendly, a little tired after work, casual

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: moshimoshi, yuki? kenta da kedo.
lines.ja: もしもし、ユキ？健太だけど。
lines.kana: もしもし、ゆき？けんただけど。
lines.english: Hello, Yuki? It's Kenta.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ashita na n da kedo, gomen, dame ni natchatta.
lines.ja: 明日なんだけど、ごめん、ダメになっちゃった。
lines.kana: あしたなんだけど、ごめん、だめになっちゃった。
lines.english: About tomorrow... sorry, it's not going to work out.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: ashita mo shigoto ga haitchatte. ima mo mada shigoto shiteru n da.
lines.ja: 明日も仕事が入っちゃって。今もまだ仕事してるんだ。
lines.kana: あしたもしごとがはいっちゃって。いまもまだしごとしてるんだ。
lines.english: I've got work tomorrow too now. I'm actually still working right now.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: demo, ashita no yoru wa daijoubu. uchi ni konai?
lines.ja: でも、明日の夜は大丈夫。うちに来ない？

questions.english: What happens in this story?

choices.english: The customer asks about a cake, buys it, and decides not to get a coffee.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-4: the customer asks what the item is and how much it costs. Line 5: she orders it plus 'are'. Line 6: the staff checks 'kono keeki to, koohii desu ne'. Line 7: 'a, koohii desu ka' shows she has just learned 'are' is coffee, and 'koohii wa ii desu' means no coffee. Line 8: 'keeki dake' means just the cake. Lines 9-10: she pays and gets it. B is what she first ordered, before she changed her mind. C is wrong because she asks about the cake, not the coffee, and she does buy something.

questions.english: At the start, the customer asks 'sore wa nan desu ka?' What is 'sore'?
questions.ja: 「それは何ですか？」の「それ」は、何でしたか？
questions.kana: 「それはなんですか？」の「それ」は、なんでしたか？
questions.romaji: "sore wa nan desu ka?" no "sore" wa, nan deshita ka?

choices.english: A coffee cake
A cup of matcha tea
A matcha cake

questions.explanation: Line 2: the staff checks which one ('dore desu ka? a, kore desu ka?') and then says 'matcha no keeki desu yo', so it's a matcha cake. The customer repeats it in line 3. Coffee only comes up later as a separate drink (line 6), and no one orders matcha to drink.

questions.english: Why does the customer get only the cake, not the coffee?
questions.ja: どうして、ケーキだけなんですか？
questions.kana: どうして、ケーキだけなんですか？
questions.romaji: doushite, keeki dake na n desu ka?

choices.english: The coffee costs four hundred yen.
She already had coffee today.
The café has no coffee today.

questions.explanation: Line 7: 'kyou wa mou nonda n desu' means she already drank some today, and 'n desu' marks it as her reason. Line 8: the staff confirms 'keeki dake'. Four hundred yen is the cake's price (lines 4 and 8), and the café does have coffee: the staff confirms it as part of her order in line 6.

questions.english: The staff says 'hai, kono keeki to, koohii desu ne.' What is the staff doing with 'desu ne'?
questions.ja: 「このケーキと、コーヒーですね」って、何ですか？
questions.kana: 「このケーキと、コーヒーですね」って、なんですか？
questions.romaji: "kono keeki to, koohii desu ne" tte, nan desu ka?

choices.english: Telling her the cake comes with a free coffee.
Asking if she would like a coffee too.
Checking her order: 'this cake and a coffee, right?'

questions.explanation: Line 5: the customer orders 'sono keeki to, are'. Line 6: the staff repeats the order back with 'desu ne'. 'ne' here is checking: 'that's right, isn't it?' Telling her something new would be 'desu yo' (like line 2, 'matcha no keeki desu yo'), and a plain question would be 'desu ka'. She already ordered it ('are'), so the staff isn't offering coffee or adding it free. Because the staff checks, she hears that 'are' is coffee and changes her mind in line 7 ('a, koohii desu ka').

questions.english: The staff member tells you 'matcha no keeki desu yo. nani ni shimasu ka?' You'd like one. What could you say back?
questions.ja: 抹茶のケーキですよ。何にしますか？
questions.kana: まっちゃのケーキですよ。なににしますか？
questions.romaji: matcha no keeki desu yo. nani ni shimasu ka?
questions.answer: Politely order it, e.g. 'jaa, sore o onegai shimasu.' or 'jaa, sore ni shimasu.'

modelAnswers.romaji: jaa, sore o onegai shimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: じゃあ、それをお願いします。
modelAnswers.english: OK then, I'll have that, please.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii desu ne. jaa, sore ni shimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: いいですね。じゃあ、それにします。
modelAnswers.english: That sounds good. Then I'll go with that.

questions.explanation: The customer does this in line 5: 'jaa' plus the item plus 'o onegai shimasu' is the basic polite way to order. The staff is near the cake, so you call it 'sore' (that one, by you). 'ii desu ne' shares a reaction (that sounds nice), and 'sore ni shimasu' (ni + suru) means 'I'll go with that', a common way to order that answers the staff's 'nani ni shimasu ka?' with the same words.

Mai explains the situation (n desu) and trails off on kedo without saying the request out loud, which is a polite way to ask for something. She isn't complaining (A). questions.english: Overall, how were Yuki's yesterday and today different?
questions.ja: 昨日と今日で、何が変わりましたか。
questions.kana: きのうときょうで、なにがかわりましたか。
questions.romaji: kinou to kyou de, nani ga kawarimashita ka?

choices.english: Yesterday was fine, but today has gone badly.
Yesterday was a long, tiring day, but today is much better.
Yesterday she stayed home, but today she went out in the rain.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-6 describe yesterday: she was exhausted (line 1), went back home in the rain for her umbrella (lines 2-3), went out again and the train didn't come (line 4), and got home at night (line 5). Line 7 says today is a lot better than yesterday (kinou yori kanari ii yo), and in line 9 she says she's fine now. A gets it backwards. C is wrong because she did go out yesterday (deta, lines 2 and 4), and today it isn't raining (line 8).

questions.english: Why did Yuki go back home after she set off yesterday?
questions.ja: ユキさんは昨日、どうしてうちに戻りましたか。
questions.kana: ゆきさんはきのう、どうしてうちにもどりましたか。
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa kinou, doushite uchi ni modorimashita ka?

choices.english: The train didn't come for a long time.
She felt too tired to go out.
It was raining and she had no umbrella.

questions.explanation: Line 2 says it was pouring (metcha ame de), and line 3 gives the reason with kara: kasa mottenakatta kara, uchi ni modotta (I didn't have my umbrella, so I went back home). The train problem (A) came later, in line 4, after she set off again with her umbrella. Being tired (B) is how she felt about the whole day (line 1), not why she went back.

questions.english: When did Yuki finally get home yesterday?
questions.ja: ユキさんは昨日、やっとうちに帰りました。それはいつでしたか。
questions.kana: ゆきさんはきのう、やっとうちにかえりました。それはいつでしたか。
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa kinou, yatto uchi ni kaerimashita. sore wa itsu deshita ka?

choices.english: Late, when it was already night.
Early, when she went back for her umbrella.
In the afternoon, before it got dark.

questions.explanation: Line 5: yatto uchi ni kaetta kedo, mou yoru datta (I finally got home, but it was already night). B is a trap: early on she only went back for her umbrella (modotta, line 3), then went out again (deta, line 4). Getting home for the day (kaetta) came at night. C is wrong because mou yoru datta means it was already night, not still light out.

questions.english: Yuki says "kasa motteru noni, ame ja nai ne." What is she saying with noni here?
questions.ja: 傘持ってるのに、雨じゃないね。この、のに、は何ですか。
questions.kana: かさもってるのに、あめじゃないね。この、のに、はなんですか。
questions.romaji: kasa motteru noni, ame ja nai ne. kono, noni, wa nan desu ka?

choices.english: She's glad she has her umbrella, since it might rain later.
She has her umbrella this time, and of course it isn't raining.
She's annoyed that she forgot her umbrella again.

questions.explanation: Line 8. -noni means 'even though... and yet': things turned out the opposite of what you'd expect, often with a small grumble. Yesterday she had no umbrella and it poured (lines 2-3). Today she has one (motteru) and it isn't raining. With ne she shares the joke with her friend. A misses the contrast that noni marks, and C is wrong because motteru means she has it with her today.

questions.english: Yuki tells you about her two days and ends with "jaa, itadakimasu!" What could you say back to her?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、じゃあ、いただきますって。ユキさんに、どうぞ。
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、じゃあ、いただきますって。ゆきさんに、どうぞ。
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, jaa, itadakimasu tte. yuki-san ni, douzo.
questions.answer: Feel for her rough day (for example otsukare, or say yesterday was bad), say you're glad today is better, and maybe join in with itadakimasu.

modelAnswers.romaji: otsukare! kyou wa yokatta ne.
modelAnswers.ja: お疲れ！今日はよかったね。
modelAnswers.english: Sounds exhausting! Glad today's better.

modelAnswers.romaji: kinou wa dame datta ne. jaa, watashi mo itadakimasu!
modelAnswers.ja: 昨日はだめだったね。じゃあ、私もいただきます！
modelAnswers.english: Yesterday was a write-off, huh. Okay, I'll dig in too!

questions.explanation: Lines 1-6 give you something to sympathize with (a tiring day, rain, going back for the umbrella, the train), and lines 7-9 tell you today is better and she's fine now. Line 10 (jaa, itadakimasu) means you're about to eat together, so you can answer with otsukare, say you're glad today is better (yokatta ne), or add your own itadakimasu.

questions.english: What do Kenta and Mai decide to do with everyone tomorrow?
questions.ja: ケンタさんとマイさんは、明日、みんなで何をしますか。
questions.kana: けんたさんとまいさんは、あした、みんなでなにをしますか。
questions.romaji: kenta-san to mai-san wa, ashita, minna de nani o shimasu ka?

choices.english: Go to the beach with everyone.
Have hot pot at Mai's place.
Go shopping together.

questions.explanation: Kenta suggests the beach in line 1, but rain is coming tomorrow (line 8), so Mai invites everyone to her place for hot pot (line 10). Line 16 confirms it: 'ashita, uchi de nabe yaru ne!'. The beach (A) is dropped. Shopping (C) is only the job Kenta takes on beforehand (line 13).

questions.english: Why is the beach no good tomorrow?
questions.ja: 明日、なんで海はダメなんですか。
questions.kana: あした、なんでうみはだめなんですか。
questions.romaji: ashita, nande umi wa dame na n desu ka?

choices.english: Mai is busy tomorrow.
Not everyone can come.
It's going to rain.

questions.explanation: In line 6 Mai says the beach might be no good. Kenta asks 'nande?' (line 7), and in line 8 she says 'ashita, ame ni naru n da tte': it's going to rain. Mai isn't busy tomorrow (A): in line 4 she says today doesn't work but tomorrow is fine. Whether everyone is coming is only something Mai will ask about later (line 14), so B is wrong.

questions.english: What does Kenta say he'll do ahead of time?
questions.ja: ケンタさんは、何をしときますか。
questions.kana: けんたさんは、なにをしときますか。
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, nani o shitokimasu ka?

choices.english: Do the shopping.
Ask everyone if they're coming.
Bring a pot to Mai's place.

questions.explanation: Line 13: 'boku, kaimono shitoku yo'. The -toku ending means doing it ahead of time. Asking everyone (B) is what Mai will do (line 14). Kenta doesn't bring a pot (C): he checks that Mai already has one, and she says 'un, aru yo' (lines 15-16).

questions.english: Mai says 'kono mae mo, minna kita yo ne?' What is she doing with 'yo ne'?
questions.ja: マイさんの「この前も、みんな来たよね？」。この「よね」は、何ですか。
questions.kana: まいさんの「このまえも、みんなきたよね？」。この「よね」は、なんですか。
questions.romaji: mai-san no "kono mae mo, minna kita yo ne?" kono "yo ne" wa, nan desu ka?

choices.english: Telling Kenta something he doesn't know yet.
Checking something she expects Kenta remembers too.
Wondering to herself whether everyone came last time.

questions.explanation: Line 12. 'Yo ne' asks the listener to confirm something both people already know. Mai is sure Kenta remembers that everyone came over last time too, so they'll fit. That answers his worry in line 11, and he confirms with 'a, un' in line 13. Plain 'yo' would be telling him something new (A). Wondering (C) is 'kana', as in Kenta's 'minna hairu kana?' in line 11.

questions.english: Mai asks 'uchi kuru? minna de nabe dekiru yo.' Will you go? What could you say back to her?
questions.ja: マイさんの「うち来る？みんなで鍋できるよ」。行きますか。

questions.romaji: mai-san no "uchi kuru? minna de nabe dekiru yo." ikimasu ka?

modelAnswers.romaji: un, iku iku! arigatou.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、行く行く！ありがとう。

speakers.name: Yuki

questions.english: What did Sora do today?
questions.ja: 今日、ソラさんは何をしましたか？
questions.kana: きょう、そらさんはなにをしましたか？
questions.romaji: kyou, sora-san wa nani o shimashita ka?

choices.english: He stayed up until morning playing games with Kenji.
He visited Yuki's home, had lunch with her family, and then left.
He helped Yuki change her room, and then they went out to eat.

questions.explanation: In lines 1-2 Sora greets Yuki's mother and she invites him in. Lines 10-14 are the lunch, and in line 15 he thanks them for the meal and leaves. Kenji was the one gaming till morning (line 8). Yuki's room has changed (lines 4-5), but nobody says Sora helped, and they eat at home ('ohiru dekita yo', line 10).

questions.english: What was Kenji doing last night?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは昨日、何をやってたんですか？
questions.kana: けんじさんはきのう、なにをやってたんですか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa kinou, nani o yatteta n desu ka?

choices.english: Working until morning.
Changing his room around.
Playing games until morning.

questions.explanation: Line 8: 'datte kinou, asa made geemu yatteta n da yo' means he was playing games till morning. Work comes up only for Sora (lines 15-16), and the room that changed is Yuki's (lines 4-5).

questions.english: Why does Sora leave after lunch?

questions.kana: そらさんは、どうしてもういくんですか？
questions.romaji: sora-san wa, doushite mou iku n desu ka?

choices.english: He has work today.
He stayed up until morning yesterday and is tired.
It's already noon and he's running late.

questions.explanation: Line 15: 'kyou wa shigoto ga aru node' gives his reason with -node (since I have work today). Yuki's mother checks it in line 16: 'oshigoto?'. Kenji was the one who stayed up till morning (line 8). 'mou hiru da yo' was Yuki teasing Kenji (line 7), not a reason for Sora to hurry.

questions.english: Yuki says 'asa made? dakara, kenji wa mada asa na wake da.' What does she mean with '... wake da'?
questions.ja: ユキさんの「だから、ケンジはまだ朝なわけだ」。この「わけだ」は、何ですか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんの「だから、けんじはまだあさなわけだ」。この「わけだ」は、なんですか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san no "dakara, kenji wa mada asa na wake da". kono "wake da" wa, nan desu ka?

choices.english: She's telling Kenji that it's still morning.
She has just worked out why Kenji is acting as if it's still morning.
She's asking Kenji whether he really played games until morning.

questions.explanation: Line 9: wake da states a conclusion that explains something ('so that's why / no wonder'). Kenji has just said he played games till morning (line 8), so it now makes sense to Yuki that he's still in 'morning' mode at noon and says ohayou. She isn't telling him it's morning: she has just said 'mou hiru da yo' (line 7). It isn't a question either: her only question is 'asa made?', and he has already told her.

questions.english: Yuki's mother offers Sora more food: 'mada aru kara, mou sukoshi douzo.' What could you say back to her?
questions.ja: まだあるから、もう少しどうぞ。
questions.kana: まだあるから、もうすこしどうぞ。
questions.romaji: mada aru kara, mou sukoshi douzo.

choices.english: She goes to work, then has dinner out with Yuki as they planned.
She goes to work, but Yuki moves their dinner to tomorrow, so Mai eats at home.
She stays home because of the rain, and Yuki comes over in the evening.

questions.explanation: In line 2 Mai tells her mother she's eating out with Yuki today ('kyou wa yuki to tabete kuru kara ne'). In line 14 Yuki calls to say today is off and asks about tomorrow, and Mai agrees in line 15 ('ashita ne!'). In line 17 her mother says 'kyou wa uchi de taberu n da': she's eating at home tonight, and lines 18-20 are that dinner. A was only the plan. C is wrong: rain is only forecast (line 3), Mai goes out in the morning and later leaves work (lines 1-2 and 11), and Yuki only phones (lines 13-16).

questions.kana: なんで、まいさんはさとうさんのかさをもってるんですか。
questions.romaji: nande, mai-san wa satou-san no kasa o motteru n desu ka?

choices.english: It's going to rain today, and she doesn't have one.
It's already raining, so she asks to borrow one.
She lent him hers yesterday, and he's giving it back.

questions.explanation: In line 3 Satou-san says 'kyou wa ame ni narimasu yo' (it's going to rain) and asks if she has an umbrella. In line 4 she says 'iie, mottemasen', and in line 5 he gives her one: 'jaa, kore, douzo', since he has another at home. B is wrong because it isn't raining yet ('ame ni narimasu' means it will rain), and he offers without being asked. C is wrong: he asks whether she has one (line 3) and says he still has one at home (line 5), so it is his own spare. Mai's surprised 'e, ii n desu ka?' (line 6) shows she is being given something, not getting hers back. His 'kinou wa arigatou gozaimashita' (line 7) is only his reply to her thanks.

questions.english: Why does Yuki cancel tonight's dinner?

questions.kana: ゆきさんは、なんできょうだめになったんですか。
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, nande kyou dame ni natta n desu ka?

choices.english: It's going to rain tonight.
She has to eat at home with her family.
She still has quite a lot of work.

questions.explanation: Line 14: 'shigoto ga mada kanari atte, kyou dame ni natchatta'. Her work isn't done yet, and the -te form (atte) gives the reason. Rain (A) is what Satou-san talked about that morning (line 3). Eating at home (B) is what happens to Mai (line 17), not Yuki.

questions.english: Mai thanks Satou-san for the umbrella, and he says 'iie, kochira koso, kinou wa arigatou gozaimashita.' What does he mean by 'kochira koso' here?
questions.ja: 「いいえ、こちらこそ、昨日はありがとうございました。」佐藤さんの「こちらこそ」って、何ですか。
questions.kana: 「いいえ、こちらこそ、きのうはありがとうございました。」さとうさんの「こちらこそ」って、なんですか。
questions.romaji: "iie, kochira koso, kinou wa arigatou gozaimashita." satou-san no "kochira koso" tte, nan desu ka?

choices.english: "No, I'm the one who should thank you" for something Mai did yesterday.
"Nice to meet you too": he's meeting Mai for the first time.
"Take care": he wants her to be careful in the rain.

questions.explanation: In line 6 Mai thanks him with 'sumimasen!'. In line 7 he answers 'iie' (no need), then 'kochira koso' turns the thanks back to her: I'm the one who should be grateful. He says what for: 'kinou wa arigatou gozaimashita' (thanks for yesterday). B is kochira koso's other job, 'likewise' after yoroshiku, which Sora uses at a first meeting in line 10. But Satou-san already knows Mai: he greets her by name in line 3 and thanks her for yesterday. C is what 'ki o tsukete' means, the next thing he says in line 7, not kochira koso.

questions.english: Kenta brings his friend over and says to you, 'chotto ii? boku no tomodachi no sora.' You've never met Sora before. What could you say to Sora?
questions.ja: ちょっといい？僕の友達のソラ。
questions.kana: ちょっといい？ぼくのともだちのそら。
questions.romaji: chotto ii? boku no tomodachi no sora.
questions.answer: Greet Sora as a first meeting: konnichiwa and/or hajimemashite, then yoroshiku (casual, maybe with ne) or yoroshiku onegai shimasu (polite).

questions.explanation: This is the moment in lines 8-10. Mai answers casually ('a, konnichiwa! hajimemashite, mai desu. yoroshiku ne.') because Sora is a friend's friend her own age. The polite 'yoroshiku onegai shimasu' also works with anyone. Expect Sora to answer 'kochira koso, yoroshiku' (line 10).

booking, reservation (yoyaku suru: to book; yoyaku shitoita: had booked ahead)

questions.english: What happened on Yuki's trip to the mountains?
questions.ja: 山で、ユキさんに何がありましたか。
questions.kana: やまで、ゆきさんになにがありましたか。
questions.romaji: yama de, yuki-san ni nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: It wasn't very cold, and she came home a day early.
It was super cold but great, and her train didn't run, so she got back late.
It was super cold, and she missed her train because she stayed in a hot spring.

questions.explanation: Lines 2-4: it was super cold ('metcha samukatta', 'motto da yo, motto!'). Lines 2 and 15-16: it was still really great ('sugoku yokatta', 'sore sore!'). Lines 9-12: she was still there yesterday because the train she'd booked didn't run ('denakatta', line 10), and it finally ran today (line 12). A is wrong because it was super cold, not mild, and she came back late, not early. C is wrong because she didn't miss the train. It didn't run at all.

questions.english: How cold was it in the mountains?
questions.ja: 山は、少し寒かったですか、かなり寒かったですか。
questions.kana: やまは、すこしさむかったですか、かなりさむかったですか。
questions.romaji: yama wa, sukoshi samukatta desu ka, kanari samukatta desu ka?

choices.english: Only a little colder than here.
Not cold at all.
Way, way colder than here.

questions.explanation: In line 3 Kenta says it's 'sukoshi samui' (a bit cold) here today and asks if the mountains were just a little colder ('mou chotto samukatta dake?'). In line 4 Yuki corrects him: 'mou chotto ja nai yo! motto da yo, motto!' (not a little, way more) and 'kanari samukute' (it was quite cold, so...). Line 2 ('metcha samukatta') and line 16 ('sukoshi ja nakute, metcha samui') say the same thing. A is Kenta's guess, which she rejects. B picks up Kenta's question 'samukunakatta?' in line 1, but she says 'metcha samukatta'.

questions.english: Were there many hot springs, and did Yuki go in a lot of them or just a few?
questions.ja: 山に、温泉は結構ありましたか。ユキさんは、かなり入りましたか、少しだけ入りましたか。
questions.kana: やまに、おんせんはけっこうありましたか。ゆきさんは、かなりはいりましたか、すこしだけはいりましたか。
questions.romaji: yama ni, onsen wa kekkou arimashita ka? yuki-san wa, kanari hairimashita ka, sukoshi dake hairimashita ka?

choices.english: There were quite a few, and she went in a lot of them.
There were only a few, so she kept going to the same one.
There were quite a few, but she only went in her favourite.

questions.explanation: In line 5 Kenta asks 'onsen, kekkou atta no?' (were there quite a few?). In line 6 Yuki says 'un, kekkou atta yo. kanari haitta': yes, quite a few, and she went in quite a lot of them. B contradicts 'kekkou atta'. Lines 7-8 also rule out C: Kenta asks 'dono onsen ga yokatta?' and she picks 'kinou haitta onsen', the one she went in yesterday, out of several she tried.

questions.english: Yuki says 'densha, yoyaku shitoita noni, denakatta n da yo.' What is she expressing with 'noni'?
questions.ja: ユキさんの「電車、予約しといたのに、出なかったんだよ」。この「のに」は、何ですか。
questions.kana: ゆきさんの「でんしゃ、よやくしといたのに、でなかったんだよ」。この「のに」は、なんですか。
questions.romaji: yuki-san no "densha, yoyaku shitoita noni, denakatta n da yo." kono "noni" wa, nan desu ka?

choices.english: She's giving the reason the train didn't run.
She booked ahead, and it still went wrong, so she's annoyed.
She's wondering whether the train will run today.

questions.explanation: Line 10. 'Noni' means 'even though... and yet'. It marks a result that goes against what should have happened, and it often carries annoyance. Booking ahead ('shitoita', did it in advance) was her planning, and the train not running is the letdown. In line 11 Kenta echoes 'yoyaku shitoita noni?' to share her surprise. A reason (A) would use 'kara' or 'node', which sound a bit like 'noni' but mean 'because'. 'yoyaku shitoita kara, denakatta' would make her booking the cause, which makes no sense. Wondering (C) would use 'kana', like 'dono onsen kana...' in line 8, and the train did run today (line 12).

questions.english: At the end, Yuki says 'kenta mo itte mite. demo, sukoshi ja nakute, metcha samui kara ne.' If you were Kenta, would you go? What could you say back?
questions.ja: 「ケンタも行ってみて。でも、少しじゃなくて、めっちゃ寒いからね。」ケンタさんは、行ってみますか。
questions.kana: 「けんたもいってみて。でも、すこしじゃなくて、めっちゃさむいからね。」けんたさんは、いってみますか。

questions.english: What happens in this conversation?
questions.ja: 何がありましたか？
questions.kana: なにがありましたか？
questions.romaji: nani ga arimashita ka?

choices.english: Kimura-san sent the email to the wrong person, so Yamada-san never got the new handout.
Tanaka-san copied yesterday's handout, and Kimura-san found the mistake.
Kimura-san copied the old handout because Tanaka-san had emailed himself by mistake.

questions.explanation: Line 3: what Kimura-san copied (watashi ga kopii shita no) wasn't kesa no shiryou (this morning's handout). It was kinou no (yesterday's). Line 4: Tanaka-san emailed everyone (minasan ni meeru shimashita). In line 6 he finds the email didn't go to her (kimura-san ni ja nakatta desu), because he sent it to himself (jibun ni meeru shichaimashita). Line 8 sums it up: sorede, kinou no o kopii shichatta wake desu ne. A is wrong because Tanaka-san sent the email, not Kimura-san, and Yamada-san did get it (line 5, yamada-san ni wa kimashita). B is wrong because Kimura-san made the copies (line 3, watashi ga kopii shita no), and the mistake Tanaka-san finds is his own (line 6).

questions.english: Who did this morning's email reach?
questions.ja: 今朝のメールは、誰に来ましたか？
questions.kana: けさのメールは、だれにきましたか？
questions.romaji: kesa no meeru wa, dare ni kimashita ka?

choices.english: It reached Yamada-san, but not Kimura-san.
It reached Kimura-san, but not Yamada-san.
It reached nobody. Tanaka-san never sent it.

questions.explanation: Line 5: yamada-san ni wa kimashita (polite past) says it came to Yamada-san, and demo, watashi ni wa konakatta n desu yo (past negative) says it never came to Kimura-san. In line 6 Tanaka-san checks with kimasen deshita ka? ('it didn't come?'), then realises kimura-san ni ja nakatta desu: the email didn't go to her. B is the reverse: line 5 says Yamada-san got it (kimashita) and Kimura-san didn't (konakatta n desu yo). C is wrong because Tanaka-san did send it to everyone (line 4, minasan ni meeru shimashita). Only the one meant for Kimura-san went to him instead (line 6, jibun ni meeru shichaimashita).

questions.english: At the end, who is going to make the copies of this morning's handout?
questions.ja: 今朝の資料のコピーは、誰がしますか？
questions.kana: けさのしりょうのコピーは、だれがしますか？
questions.romaji: kesa no shiryou no kopii wa, dare ga shimasu ka?

choices.english: Kimura-san, right away, because the meeting is soon.
Tanaka-san, by himself.
Yamada-san, who already got this morning's handout by email.

questions.explanation: Line 13: Kimura-san asks kopii wa dare ga shimasu ka? ('who's going to do the copies?') and offers to do them herself (watashi, ima kara yatte mimasu). In line 14 Tanaka-san says iie, sore wa dame desu yo, so he won't let her, and then kopii wa jibun de shimasu, 'I'll do the copies myself.' In line 15 she accepts with jaa, onegai shimasu. A is wrong because her offer is turned down. C is wrong because Yamada-san is only mentioned as someone the email reached (line 5).

questions.english: Kimura-san says, "a, dakara watashi ni wa konakatta wake desu ne." What does she mean by "wake desu"?
questions.ja: 木村さんの「だから私には来なかったわけですね」。この「わけです」は、何ですか？
questions.kana: きむらさんの「だからわたしにはこなかったわけですね」。この「わけです」は、なんですか？
questions.romaji: kimura-san no "dakara watashi ni wa konakatta wake desu ne". kono "wake desu" wa, nan desu ka?

choices.english: She is giving Tanaka-san an excuse: the email never came to her, so it isn't her fault.
She is wondering why the email never came to her.
She is putting it together from what he just said: so that's why the email never reached her.

questions.explanation: Line 7: wake desu draws a conclusion from facts you've just heard, like 'so that's why' or 'no wonder'. In line 6 Tanaka-san has just said jibun ni meeru shichaimashita (he emailed himself), so Kimura-san puts it together, and ne checks that conclusion with him. A is what she did in line 5 with demo, watashi ni wa konakatta n desu yo, where n desu yo gives him a reason he didn't know. By line 7 she already knows the email didn't come and is working out why. B is what Tanaka-san did in line 6 with doushite desu ka ne (wondering). wake desu answers that wondering. It doesn't add to it.

questions.english: Tanaka-san says, "sumimasen deshita. watashi ga warui n desu." What could you say back to him?
questions.ja: すみませんでした。私が悪いんです。
questions.kana: すみませんでした。わたしがわるいんです。
questions.romaji: sumimasen deshita. watashi ga warui n desu.
questions.answer: Start with iie, then reassure him (daijoubu desu yo) or apologise back with kochira koso.

modelAnswers.romaji: iie, daijoubu desu yo.
modelAnswers.ja: いいえ、大丈夫ですよ。
modelAnswers.english: No, it's all right.

modelAnswers.romaji: iie, kochira koso sumimasen deshita.
modelAnswers.ja: いいえ、こちらこそすみませんでした。
modelAnswers.english: No, I'm the one who should apologise.

questions.explanation: In line 8 Tanaka-san apologises and takes the blame. In line 9 Kimura-san answers iie. tanaka-san wa warukunai desu yo ('No. It's not your fault, Tanaka-san'). In Japanese the usual reply to an apology is iie first, then something kind. daijoubu desu yo reassures him. kochira koso sumimasen deshita apologises back ('no, I'm the one...'). Tanaka-san uses kochira koso the same way in line 12.

Friends are coming over for Kenta's birthday, so the two of them get the place ready.

questions.explanation: In line 4 Kenta says 'minna ga uchi ni kuru n da': everyone is coming to their place. Sora checks this in line 5 with 'boku-tachi no uchi ni?'. In line 8 Kenta asks 'kyou, dare no tanjoubi?', and in line 9 Sora realizes it's Kenta's birthday ('kenta no!?'). Lines 10-16 split up the jobs. A is wrong because Yuki is one of the guests coming to them, and nobody goes to her place. C is wrong because it's Kenta's birthday, not Sora's, and Sora is the one buying the cake (lines 11 and 15).

questions.kana: けんたさんは、いまいるへやをやって、なにをやりますか。
questions.romaji: kenta-san wa, ima iru heya o yatte, nani o yarimasu ka?

Go to the shop with Sora.
Clean his own room.

questions.explanation: Line 14: 'boku wa koko yatte, jibun no heya yaru'. The -te on 'yatte' links the two steps: first here (koko), then his own room (jibun no heya). Buying the cake (A) is Sora's job (lines 11 and 15), and Sora goes out alone ('ima kara dete', line 15), so B is wrong too. Kenta's offer in line 16 to do Sora's room comes on top of this plan. questions.kana: そらさんは、なにをしないんですか。

choices.english: Clean his own room.
Go out today.
Buy the cake.

questions.explanation: Line 15: 'boku no heya wa souji shinai yo'. Plain 'shinai' here means 'I'm not going to do it', and he backs it up with 'datte, minna boku no heya ni wa hairanai shi' (the guests won't go in his room anyway). He does go out (B): 'ima kara dete' in line 15. He offers to buy the cake (C) in line 11. In line 3 he thought they weren't doing anything today ('nani mo shinai yo ne?'), but that changes once he hears about the birthday.

questions.english: When Sora asks who's coming, Kenta says 'yuki to mai. ato, daiki mo.' What does 'ato' do here?

questions.romaji: "yuki to mai. ato, daiki mo." kono "ato" wa, nan desu ka?

It adds one more person to the list.

Kenta does the same in line 10, where 'ato, koko to heya no souji mo mada' adds the unfinished cleaning to 'keeki ga mada nai'. It doesn't mean 'later' here (A). Nothing is said about when anyone arrives. If Kenta weren't sure (C), he would say something like 'daiki mo kuru kana'.

questions.explanation: In line 15 Sora uses 'datte' to excuse himself: the guests (minna) won't go into his room anyway. The first answer pushes back with 'dame' and gives the reason with 'n da yo', reminding him that everyone is coming today. The second answer accepts, like Kenta does in line 16, and uses -toku ('I'll get it done for you').
